# F15 and F16 fixed, F17 carried, and the fourth figure finding placed as a rule

The third review returned the ticket on F15 and raised F16 and F17. All three are
answered here, and none needed production code: this round is the ticket file and two
measurements.

## F15, the worst placed of the four

The amendment to criterion 1 said `packages/core/db` holds eleven modules. It holds
nine, and `git ls-tree` says it held nine at SEEN-008's own merge and at both of this
ticket's own earlier commits, so the figure was never right rather than having gone
stale. That is a wrong number inside the definition of done, which is the one place a
figure cannot be allowed to be decorative.

The error claim was wrong twice over and in two directions. The amendment said "two of
them carry genuine errors", meaning two modules; the carried-forward paragraph said
`db/marketplaces.ts` "carries two genuine errors", meaning one module with two. Neither
is what the compiler says. Both figures now name a check:

- **Check 253**, `git ls-files packages/core/db`: nine files, three source modules and
  six test files.
- **Check 254**, the three source modules compiled under the four flags with an ESM
  module setting: five diagnostics, every one of them in `db/marketplaces.ts`, two
  `TS2322`, two `TS2345` and one `TS2532`, with `db/repository.ts` and `db/tables.ts`
  clean.

Worth saying what that measurement also settled, because it changes the size of the
carried work rather than only its description: with the six test files included the
count goes past a hundred, almost all `TS2532` from `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on tests
that index arrays. Whoever writes that ticket should know it is not an afternoon.

## F16, a claim that this ticket's own loop would have falsified

Two sentences in the Outcome named no check, in the paragraph that then says every
figure names one. The four weekly-report figures are gone: the report is generated from
the journal on the day it is asked for, so a number copied into the ticket is a second
answer going stale, and the sentence now says what a reader will see rather than what
somebody saw. And the `doctor` claim is corrected in the direction the reviewer spotted,
which is the sharpest thing in this round: `doctor` reports no warnings **today**, and
it will report one as soon as this ticket is inside the calibration window, because F2
and F14 both name `harness/outcome-figure-names-its-record` as the rule that would have
caught them and no such rule is written. The Outcome now says so. A ticket whose own
delivery turns one of its sentences false is a ticket that wrote the sentence wrong.

## F17 and the rule, both carried

F17 is real and its example is in the tree: `no-em-or-en-dash` and `no-euro-sign` read
only TypeScript under `apps` and `packages`, while their citations say "anywhere, in
code, docs or customer-facing copy", and `.codegraph/.gitignore` is tracked, carries an
em dash, and passes the whole set. The registry already argues the other side of this in
the entry for `harness/no-live-marketplace-host`. It is carried rather than fixed because
widening two rules to every tracked file needs the exclusion list `marketplace_hosts`
carries, and that is a rule to write deliberately and not at the end of a twelfth attempt.

And the fourth figure finding is now carried as the rule it asks for,
`harness/tdd-record-count-matches-check`. F2, F13, F14 and F15 are one defect in four
places, the tdd gate already holds a record's `red` and `green` to the checks they name,
and this is that comparison one layer in over output the journal already stores.

## What the next round does

The usual: six pairs replayed, the three measurements re-taken, the tdd record written
with every count read out of its check, the status and the boxes set, the figures
repointed, then the regression and the coverage last. `.harness-drafts/replay2.sh` and
`.harness-drafts/round6.sh` do the ten and the two. Checks 253 and 254 are this round's
own and do not need re-taking: they measure a directory this ticket does not touch.

Three reviews have now read this diff and none has questioned the rule set. Seventeen
findings, of which fourteen are closed, three are carried with their reasons, and the
one thing that keeps returning is a number that does not match the record it names.
